name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 15, 2015

 A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
 Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
 Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
 Schlicht at 5:01 p.m., on June 15, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

 A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
 by 5:00 p.m. on June 10, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
 posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
 Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

 *All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:45)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths (arrived at 5:27 p.m.)
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 RECESS

 At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were no closed session items this evening.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

City Council Minutes  1  June 15, 2015
  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Mission Viejo High School Varsity Baseball Team as "2015 CIF
  Southern Section Division 2 Champions"

  Mayor Schlicht presented commendations to the Mission Viejo High School Varsity
  Baseball Team players and coaches.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Schlicht presented a certificate of appreciation to Beth McConaughy for her
  volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Library.

P3.  Proclaim June 15, 2015, as "World Elder Abuse Awareness Day"

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Patrice Gilgan.

P4.  Presentation by Santa Margarita Water District on the Drought Response Ad Hoc
  Committee

  The City Council received the presentation from Jim Leach, Santa Margarita Water
  District External Affairs Director.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Carole Weidler, M.V.: stated that she was fortunate to volunteer on resident Margo Ferron's "Feed
'Em" team for the Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball camp. She expressed her gratitude to Ms.
Ferron and noted that the amputee children were indeed special and talented. Mrs. Weidler said
that she gained more from the volunteer opportunity than she gave and she expressed pride in
being part of a community that is so supportive of groups such as the Wounded Warriors.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: asked why the City’s Annual Report never mentions the
Nadadores. Referencing agenda item 20, she stated that she hopes the holes in the budget will be
plugged by the time it is adopted on July 6 and she asked questions about the layout of the budget
relative to the swim and dive complex.

Dr. Casey Cooper, Ph.D., M.V.: stated that Mayor Schlicht displays a pervasive pattern of behavior
that demonstrates disrespect and disregard for residents and colleagues who don't agree with
her. Dr. Cooper expressed concern with Mayor Schlicht’s actions and stated that Mission Viejo
needs a new Mayor.

City Council Minutes  2  June 15, 2015
 David Haigh, M.V.: presented a photograph of the Nadadores diving team to express their gratitude
for the City's support.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 5, 6, and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

4.  Check Register Dated May 29, 2015 in the Amount of $641,771.85

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2015

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for April 2015

  Received and filed.

11.  City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Eligibility Components

  (1) Adopted Resolution 15-26 Concerning the Status of the City of Mission Viejo General
  Plan Circulation Element and Mitigation Fee Program for the Renewed Measure M (M2)
  Program; and (2) directed staff to transmit said resolution to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA) by June 30, 2015, to maintain the City's eligibility in
City Council Minutes  3  June 15, 2015
   receiving Fiscal Year 2015-2016 Renewed Measure M (M2) local turnback revenues and
  in pursuing competitive grant funding.

12.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2015-16

  Adopted Resolution 15-27 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2015-16
  for Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).

13.  Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of Streets,
  Drainage Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes, Emergency Response and Heavy
  Equipment

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject program to Tom Bistline Construction, Inc., (A15-35)
  for the period of July 1, 2015, to June 30, 2017, in an amount not to exceed $198,000.00;
  (2) authorized the issuance of a purchase order for the period of July 1, 2015, through June
  30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $99,000.00; and (3) approved license agreement with
  Tom Bistline Construction, Inc., for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2017.

14.  Banking Services

  Authorized the City Manager/Executive Director to execute agreements with US Bank to
  provide banking services to the City for an additional three years for the period July 1,
  2015, through June 30, 2018.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Mayor Schlicht stated that she would like to make a correction to the Minutes because she
  feels they are misleading and do not contain comments made by the other Council
  Members for agenda item 18.

  Council Member Ury stated that he could support an amendment to the Minutes if the
  verbatim discussion were added to agenda item 18.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to direct the City
  Clerk to amend the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 1, 2015, by listing
  verbatim discussion for agenda item 18.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  June 15, 2015
 3.  Check Register Dated May 22, 2015 in the Amount of $2,102,334.05

  Referring to a payment made to Mission Viejo Activities Committee (MVAC) in the
  amount of $7,000, Mayor Schlicht stated that she thought the MVAC was a volunteer group
  so she would like an explanation of the expenditure.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that staff will research the payment and get back to the
  Council with a response.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Professional Services Agreement for Printing and Related Services for Outlook and
  Mission Viejo Life Publications

  Mayor Schlicht thanked the City Clerk for finding a price reduction for the City's printing
  and she shared her idea to sell advertisements to help offset the cost of the City's
  publications.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) approve the
  Professional Services Agreement with iColor Printing & Mailing, Inc.(A15- 33) for
  printing and related services for four issues of Outlook and eight issues of Mission Viejo
  Life for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2017, in the amount of $119,780; and
  (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order to iColor Printing & Mailing, Inc. for the period
  of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $59,890 pending the
  City Council's adoption of the 2015-2017 budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program – Lilley
  Planning Group

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report and answered
  the City Council Member's questions.

City Council Minutes  5  June 15, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the Agreement with Lilley Planning Group from July 1, 2015, to June 30, 2017,
  in an amount not to exceed $113,000 ($56,500 /year) for Technical Assistance.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April
  2015

  Mayor Schlicht noted that she signed the grant deed for the transfer of funds from the
  Housing Authority to the City's General Fund for the sale of Site C. She expressed concern
  that the cash payment due upon execution of the Site C sale agreement could reduce the
  cash balance in the Housing Authority by too much and could potentially cause a shortage
  for regular on-going obligations in the fund, including the remaining balances due for the
  Lennar units.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that staff did a calculation of
  the demands that will be due as well as other operating costs and that amount has already
  been deducted.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Santa Margarita Water District’s Drought Response Ad Hoc Committee

  Mayor Schlicht announced that she objects to the City's participation on the Santa
  Margarita Water District ad hoc committee because the City has three water
  districts. She said that it is her intention to form a City Water Conservation Committee
  and invite each of the water districts to participate.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht to reject the SMWD request and create a City
  committee including the three water districts. The motion died for lack of a second.

City Council Minutes  6  June 15, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to accept
  the Santa Margarita Water District's invitation to participate on the Drought Response Ad
  Hoc Committee.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Schlicht appointed herself and Mayor Pro Tem Raths to serve on the Santa
  Margarita Water District's Drought Response Ad Hoc Committee.

16.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he had nothing to report.

17.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

18.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that he was out of town and missed the last meeting of
  the OCTA Board of Directors.

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report / AB1217 (Daly)

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (CONTINUED)

Anna Warner, M.V.: asked about the process for allowing building inspectors to issue permits
when the property is in violation of the building code.

STAFF REPORTS

20.  Review of 2015-17 Proposed Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented an overview of the proposed
  2015-17 Budget and answered the City Council Member's questions.

City Council Minutes  7  June 15, 2015
   Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has been requesting, for four years, that staff or
  prior City Council Members conduct a study and identify ways to reduce police costs. He
  proposed the formation of a coalition of Orange County City Managers to do identify areas
  to reduce costs.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 15-28 to Authorize Appropriations Commencing July 1, 2015, Based on Prior
  Year Spending and the Proposed Budget, Until Such Time as the 2015-17 Budget is
  Adopted.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct staff
  to establish a separate object line item for economic development in the amount of
  $160,000 (as outlined in the staff report) for the hiring of external consultants and for other
  economic development needs.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum announced that regional planning groups such as the Southern
 California Association of Governments (SCAG) and the Orange County Council of
 Governments (OCCOG) are seeking the public's input on transportation matters. She invited
 the community to attend meetings on June 18 from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the Aliso Viejo City
 Council Chamber, on June 23 from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at Cal State Fullerton, and on June 25 from
 12:00 to 2:00 p.m. at OCTA offices. Council Member Bucknum asked the City Clerk if she can
 include information on these meetings on the City's website. She also encouraged residents to
 attend and speak up on transportation issues to help create mobility and to minimize the impacts

City Council Minutes  8  June 15, 2015
  on Mission Viejo streets. Council Member Bucknum provided details on her attendance at
 recent events including the Wounded Warriors Camp exhibition baseball game, the Mission
 Viejo Chamber breakfast, a Southern California Association of Governments meeting where she
 participated on the Economic and Human Development Committee, the Mission Viejo
 Community of Character high school senior recognition ceremony, the 2015 Relay for Life, and
 the Rotary’s charity benefit event.

 Council Member Ury

 Council Member Ury thanked staff and his colleagues for putting together a very comprehensive
 draft budget. He stated that there was a lot of work that went on behind the scenes and the
 amount of time Mission Viejo staff puts into the budget is disproportionate to most cities of the
 same size. Council Member Ury expressed his apologies for missing several meetings when he
 was out of town recently.

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked the City Manager and his staff for putting together a very
 responsible and balanced budget. He stated that he wishes that national leaders would take note
 on what Mission Viejo does and get their budgets in line. Mayor Pro Tem Raths discussed his
 attendance at the Rotary Club’s Texas Hold 'Em event where more than 150 attendees raised
 money for over 30 charities in the area. He noted that he had a good time and he was pleased to
 come in fourth place in the tournament. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that when he was
 elected there were a lot of empty businesses at some of the City’s malls and shopping centers
 but since the first of the year, 140 new businesses have come to Mission Viejo. In conclusion,
 Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked his colleagues for their hard work on the budget.

 Council Member Sachs

 Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

 Mayor Schlicht

 Mayor Schlicht announced that she had the joy of attending a recent preschool graduation at
 Happy Minds Kids Academy. She also shared some concerns with staff about an ongoing
 visibility problem with the traffic signal at Marathon and Robins Circle. She stated that the
 traffic light is hidden behind trees when a driver is heading south down Muirlands. Mayor
 Schlicht relayed a complaint that she has received about noise from soccer games at the
 YMCA. She asked what the parameters are and if they are allowed to play any time of day.

 Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that they are
 allowed to play soccer within certain hours and he will contact the YMCA to check on the
 matter.

 Mayor Schlicht announced that she has received a 200-signature petition from resident Lamar
 Kelsoe who is asking that streets in his neighborhood be treated with overlay rather than slurry
City Council Minutes  9  June 15, 2015
  seal. She asked the City Clerk to invite a representative from Cox to an upcoming Council
 Meeting to make a presentation on the Cox all-digital transition and lastly, she asked Council
 Member Ury to forward his email regarding Care Ambulance. Mayor Schlicht announced that
 the Mission Viejo High School Diablos girls’ softball team was number one in the nation all
 year and sadly, lost their last game. The two coaches were chosen as the Orange County Register
 Coaches of the Year and she would like to extend an invitation to the coaches and entire team
 to come to a City Council meeting to be recognized. In closing, Mayor Schlicht read a quote
 from King Solomon: “I know that there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do
 good while they live.”

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 8:47 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, July 6, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of July 6, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  June 15, 2015
